Saddle-point problems · SETTING 348

Simplex matrix games with two-sided matrix-vector products

CV_S_SIMPLEX_MATRIX_GAME

Normalized simplex-simplex matrix games with separate deterministic-risk and randomized-accuracy views. The randomized view has proved singleton-side 0/1 thresholds and explicit remaining gaps; the source adaptive-core claim is not promoted to an accepted lower bound. A full-domain KOS v3 upper is combined with exact reconstruction under the randomized target quantity.

01

Setting specification

Task

Return a pair of mixed strategies for the normalized matrix game on the two simplexes. The quality of the strategies is measured by their full saddle gap.

Solve the normalized matrix game $\min_{x\in\Delta_n}\max_{y\in\Delta_m}y^{\mathsf T}Ax$.

Admissible model

The hidden matrix is $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, with $\max_{i,j}|A_{ij}|\le1$ and public positive integers $m,n$.

$\Delta_k=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:u\ge0,\ \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}u=1\}$ for every positive integer $k$. Both strategy sets are compact and convex, and a saddle point exists.

Oracle interface

For arbitrary vectors $(x,y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m$, one query returns the exact bundle $(Ax,A^{\mathsf T}y)$. Query vectors need not be probability vectors.

One bundled left/right multiplication costs one call. A single-direction multiplication is obtained by setting the other query vector to zero. The matrix is fixed before interaction and its entries are not directly accessible.

Dimensions and strategy sets are public. The requested budget or accuracy is specified by the comparison quantity for the selected view.

Output

Return $(\widehat x,\widehat y)\in\Delta_n\times\Delta_m$. Unqueried outputs and arbitrary measurable transcript postprocessing are permitted; no certificate is required.

Loss or accuracy criterion

The full saddle gap compares the two players' best response values against the returned strategies. The deterministic fixed-budget view measures worst-case gap for its budget. The randomized target-accuracy view requires gap at most $\varepsilon$ with probability at least $2/3$.

The loss is $\operatorname{Gap}(\widehat x,\widehat y)=\max_{v\in\Delta_m}v^{\mathsf T}A\widehat x-\min_{u\in\Delta_n}\widehat y^{\mathsf T}Au$. It lies in $[0,2]$.

Resource accounting

One bundled two-sided query increments $N_{\rm matvec}$ by one. A single right or transpose product can be obtained by setting the other input to zero and is charged as one bundled call.

Use a fixed worst-case budget: calls never exceed the prespecified $N$ on any instance or random execution path. Earlier stopping within the budget is permitted.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Deterministic risk

Any measurable sequential adaptive deterministic algorithm is allowed. Queries and outputs may use the complete history, with no additional span, zero-support, communication, or memory restriction.

At public budget $N$, select one deterministic algorithm and then take the worst output gap over every admissible fixed matrix. The call cap holds on every instance:

$$ r_{\rm det}^{\star}(N;m,n)=\inf_{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{\rm det}:\,\sup_A N_{\rm matvec}(\mathcal A,A)\le N}\sup_{A\in[-1,1]^{m\times n}}\left[\max_{v\in\Delta_m}v^{\mathsf T}A\widehat x-\min_{u\in\Delta_n}\widehat y^{\mathsf T}Au\right] $$

Here $\mathfrak A_{\rm det}$ is the deterministic adaptive class declared above; $\widehat x,\widehat y$ are its feasible outputs.

View qualification. This deterministic fixed-budget risk view uses public $N\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}$ and dimensions $m,n\ge2$.

Budget convention
fixed worst-case number N of bundled two-sided products

Randomized accuracy

Arbitrary measurable sequential adaptive randomized algorithms are allowed. The private seed is independent of the hidden instance. Queries, stopping, and output may use the full history, without additional span, zero-respecting, communication, or memory restrictions.

A single algorithm is chosen from the public input and must satisfy the following guarantee for every admissible fixed matrix:

$$ \exists\mathcal A\ \forall A\in[-1,1]^{m\times n}:\quad\Pr\!\left(\max_{v\in\Delta_m}v^{\mathsf T}A\widehat x-\min_{u\in\Delta_n}\widehat y^{\mathsf T}Au\le\varepsilon\right)\ge\frac23 $$

Probability is over private algorithmic randomness only. The hidden matrix is fixed before interaction.

View qualification. This randomized accuracy view allows positive integer dimensions $m,n\ge1$. Its quantity is the smallest fixed worst-case call budget achieving $\Pr(\operatorname{Gap}(\widehat x,\widehat y)\le\varepsilon)\ge2/3$ for every admissible fixed matrix.

Budget convention
fixed_worst_case_cap

Output rule
Outputs belong to the declared space and are evaluated by this profile's METRIC. Different gaps, norms, and squared norms are not interchanged.
Resource conversion
All resource costs come from one algorithm or one hard construction. Initialization and nested calls are included.
Constants
Use the source theorem’s universal constants except where derivative order or structural budgets are explicitly fixed. Unspecified sufficient thresholds remain symbolic.
Logarithmic factors
None.
Derivation
A strategy pair with full saddle gap at most $\varepsilon$ gives a maximizing strategy with one-sided suboptimality at most $\varepsilon$. Proposition 14 of the source converts a simplex-simplex solver to an $\ell_1$-ball-simplex solver by doubling matrix width without increasing bundled matvec calls. This record is a version-specific deterministic risk lower bound. The sharper exponent is recorded separately; neither is promoted to an unrestricted randomized lower bound.
Scope qualification
The source theorem covers arbitrary adaptive deterministic queries, beyond linear-span iterations. It does not thereby give an arbitrary-randomized lower bound.
Upper bound
\[O(\sqrt{\log(n+1)\log(m+1)}/N)\]

/proofs/0/body · SHA-256 71b960f326e4ac7b3fc8ebc9c89f266531d6caa43e5e9ed513ae2b23a14256cf
In each bundled two-sided query, set the unused input vector to zero. Standard basis queries recover all columns using the number of minimizing coordinates, or all rows using the number of maximizing coordinates. Choose the smaller direction for exactly $\min\{m,n\}$ calls. The complete payoff matrix is then known, and an exact equilibrium is obtainable by the allowed uncharged internal optimization. The saddle gap is zero. Transposing the matrix to the canonical row-maximizer convention only swaps the response blocks and does not change the call count.

/proofs/2/body · SHA-256 e09bf9653307861d97604da640f27e1d4619f8e0d3b7f7a2619c464820b0e1d2
Return x=(1/n,...,1/n) and y=(1/m,...,1/m) without information calls. For any row i and column j, (Ax)_i-(A^T y)_j = sum_{k!=j} A_{ik}/n - sum_{l!=i} A_{lj}/m + (1/n-1/m)A_{ij}. The entry bound gives an upper bound (n-1)/n+(m-1)/m+|1/n-1/m| = 2-2/max(m,n). The full saddle gap is the maximum of these differences over i,j, so the same bound holds for every fixed admissible matrix. The output is feasible and deterministic, hence meets instancewise success probability at least 2/3 whenever epsilon>=2-2/max(m,n). It uses zero calls on every path. Nonnegativity of call cost implies N^*(epsilon;m,n)=0 there. The non-strict inequalities include equality. If m=n=1 the threshold and gap are zero, so every allowed epsilon>0 qualifies. This proves a sufficient zero-cost region, not necessity of the threshold for randomized zero-query methods. All constants and inequalities are exact and uniform in m,n,epsilon.

/proofs/3/proof · SHA-256 8979e58015e051c5b7064416e78f3f0335a09df942bfc0181d69b6503a8d01ed
If n<=m, query (e_j,0) for j=1,...,n; each bundled response contains the j-th column A e_j. If m<n, query (0,e_i) for i=1,...,m and read each row from A^T e_i. Each is a legal arbitrary-real-vector query and costs exactly one bundled call. The full matrix is then known. A saddle point exists by compact convex strategy sets and bilinearity; exact internal solution is uncharged in this oracle model. The returned feasible pair has gap zero on every instance and every execution, so it meets the target per-instance probability 2/3 for all positive tolerances with pathwise cap min(m,n). This is a direct derivation for q2, not an assertion that the legacy source-scoped q1 is definitionally the same quantity.

proof
/proofs/4/proof · SHA-256 e9aa2d2cd807ab4f783c2a3c97191c32e633ecad37aade2f88e4dbc6de7b41ab
Let D=max(m,n) and k_D=ceil(2D/3). Suppose first n=D>=2. For each j in [n], take A^(j) with every row identical, entry -1 in column j and +1 elsewhere. The full gap of any output equals 2(1-x_j), independent of y. If epsilon<tau_D=2-2/k_D, success requires x_j>=1-epsilon/2>1/k_D. Since the coordinates of x sum to one, at most k_D-1 indices can satisfy this for any fixed output. For a zero-query randomized output, average success over these D fixed matrices is at most (k_D-1)/D<2/3. At least one fixed matrix therefore violates the required confidence. If m=D instead, use matrices with identical columns, entry +1 in the distinguished row and -1 elsewhere. The gap is 2(1-y_i), and the same argument applies. This is an indistinguishability proof for arbitrary private randomness, without any span restriction or finite-precision assumption. If m=1, choose a uniformly random k_D-subset S of the n=D column coordinates and output its uniform distribution. Fix an arbitrary matrix and one minimizing coordinate j*. The chance that j* belongs to S is k_D/D>=2/3. Conditional on this event, the average loss in S minus its minimum is at most 2(k_D-1)/k_D=tau_D, since every entry lies in [-1,1]. Thus zero queries meet the target for epsilon>=tau_D, including equality. When n=1 use a uniformly random k_D-subset of the maximizing rows; conditional on containing a maximizing row, the maximum minus subset average has the same bound. Below tau_D, the proved one-query necessity and one-query exact reconstruction match. For D=1 the only strategy pair has gap zero, k_D=1 and tau_D=0, so all positive tolerances cost zero. The sufficiency argument requires one side to be a singleton. In general two-sided geometries only the lower for epsilon<tau_D is claimed; the region between tau_D and the deterministic uniform-strategy threshold remains unresolved here.

/proofs/5/proof · SHA-256 44d0f92f2344f73526735c796d3e88e1f8227a2fb4d076e6682712cdb27c3d24

/proofs/6/proof · SHA-256 f62148a6962773b7a8bc5cf54d7915b6ba9b2a4da950a393155e8609c6b1a863
Source premise: Karmarkar--O'Carroll--Sidford, arXiv:2601.02347v3, Theorem 1.1, states a deterministic algorithm for every normalized game of this type with tilde-O(eta^(-2/3)) matvecs. Section 1 defines an eta-solution by the complete saddle gap, and its oracle returns the pair (A^T y,Ax). Footnote 3 limits the hidden factors to polylogarithms in m,n,eta^(-1). The source's Section 7.2 proof establishes this theorem without a lower bound on dimension depending on eta. Class/output/metric map: the source class X=Delta_n, Y=Delta_m and max_{i,j}|A_{ij}|<=1 is exactly the present normalized class. Its feasible output pair is a legal target output, and its max_y y^T A xhat - min_x yhat^T A x metric is the target complete gap. Run the theorem at eta=min{epsilon,1/2}. Since eta<=epsilon, its deterministic gap guarantee implies target success probability one, hence at least 2/3, for every fixed admissible matrix. This is a one-way deterministic-witness inclusion into the randomized algorithm class; it transfers no deterministic lower bound. Oracle/cost map: the source pair query is a legal target query because the target allows arbitrary real x,y. One such source pair is answered by exactly one target bundled response (Ax,A^T y), with order exchanged internally if needed. A source implementation that requests one directional product can obtain it using one target call with the other vector zero and discard the extra response. If two directions are requested sequentially, charge the actual two calls; do not divide directional counts by two or merge adaptively dependent queries. Thus the source count is an upper bound on target calls, up to at most a fixed convention factor absorbed in C_KOS. Exact arithmetic, known-domain optimization, and computation from returned data are free in both query models. The source has a deterministic worst-case call bound, so its witness satisfies the target pathwise cap; there is no expectation-to-cap conversion. Uniform integer budget: because m,n>=1 and 0<eta<=1/2, the positive quantity ell_KOS=1+log(2mn/eta) dominates 1, log m, log n and log(1/eta). The source tilde-O bound can therefore be bounded by C_KOS eta^(-2/3) ell_KOS^(p_KOS) for fixed universal C_KOS>=1 and p_KOS>=0, increasing the constant for finite endpoint ranges. Round upward to K_KOS. For m,n>=2 use the source algorithm. When min(m,n)=1, use the separately proved one-call exact reconstruction instead, which is no greater than K_KOS. This handles singleton dimensions without relying on an entropy bound with log(1)=0. The choice eta<=1/2 also handles epsilon>=1 and avoids a false vanishing logarithmic factor. All dimensions are finite and positive, and epsilon=0 is outside the native accuracy domain. Envelope: independently, basis reconstruction costs at most min(m,n) and returns gap zero. Both witnesses are chosen using public dimensions and accuracy, so select the smaller of their public proved integer caps. This proves the displayed min bound directly for q2. The old q1 source-scoped resource record is not identified with q2, and the old narrow b2 record is not needed for the new envelope. On every nonzero comparison updated here, 0<epsilon<2; consequently epsilon/4<=eta<=epsilon and the same upper is written min{min(m,n),tilde-O(epsilon^(-2/3))}, with only the stated positive dimension/precision logarithms suppressed. Existing exact zero and exact one-query rows are sharper and remain selected unchanged. This proves only an upper bound; the separate claimed randomized growing lower remains excluded.

Disjoint union of native contracts: deterministic_risk q1 is minimax full saddle-gap risk for integer N>=1 and m,n>=2; randomized_accuracy q2 is the least fixed worst-case bundled-call cap for epsilon>0 and positive integer m,n with instancewise success >=2/3. Its distinct q1 is only a source-scoped resource statement. All instances have |A_ij|<=1. Joint variation is within each view, never between incompatible costs. Derived d=n+m is redundant; source q is selected through epsilon, not an independent asymptotic budget. Tracking q and epsilon_0 in q2 metadata does not make them independent joint inputs. The fixed-public-input wording of deterministic q1 defines pointwise minimax values and its tracked N,m,n vary jointly here; no metadata edit is required.

/joint_analysis/domain_map/cells/7/note · SHA-256 5449d4674df6113362cde822346485ef323635ee4094b7fe6be9e21655e7f546
The new complete KOS v3-to-q2 proof gives a deterministic pathwise cap in every positive dimension, independent of the source lower-bound window H. Take the minimum with the separately proved q2 basis-reconstruction cap. Explicitly the integer envelope is min{min(m,n),ceil(C_KOS eta^(-2/3) ell_KOS^(p_KOS))}. The displayed tilde form is valid on this row because 0<epsilon<2; eta=min{epsilon,1/2}. This changes only the upper side and leaves all lower exclusions and endpoint predicates intact.

/joint_analysis/domain_map/partition_argument · SHA-256 f273f801cb98974a718f4f6da00a71e334d80188bd37baff5821918ebb1c39fc
The deterministic risk view and its prior domain accounting remain separate. In randomized_accuracy: D=1 is zero; if min(m,n)=1, tau_D divides exact zero and one-query cells. For min(m,n)>=2, split epsilon>=u_D, tau_D<=epsilon<u_D, and epsilon<tau_D, then split the last cell by H. Since tau_D<=u_D, the primary randomized cells are disjoint and exhaustive. The legacy source-scoped q1 remains unselected; its identity is not merged with q2.
